key_insight: Adaptive hyperreduction accelerates neural constitutive model discovery while preserving identification accuracy as network weights change during training.
engineering_relevance: The approach makes finite element model updating more affordable for learning material laws from structural experiments with arbitrary geometries and sparse or noisy measurements.
method: Reduce the displacement space using proper orthogonal decomposition.
Adapt the reduced basis and energy-conserving element sampling during optimization, using reduced-model adjoint sensitivities.
Learn a neural strain-energy law that is polyconvex, coercive, and non-negative by construction.
evidence_signal: Across two experimental datasets and one synthetic 3D example, the method reproduced reaction forces and predicted displacement fields; two-phase training fell from 9 hours to 41 minutes without reported accuracy loss.
watch_item: Accuracy during training depends on adapting both the reduced basis and sampled elements as the constitutive model evolves.
paper_title: Hyperreduction accelerates finite element model updating for the discovery of neural materials
